display_contract.front: Arabic script only; no translation, English question, transliteration, definition, or hint.
display_contract.back: All translations, definitions, examples, grammar/register data, metadata, and eight layered fields.
display_contract.retrieval_direction: Arabic -> meaning/use first; alternate representations are scheduled separately.

source_basis.note: Concepts were learned before the public-source migration; these public/open sources validate and reinforce the same material.

cards.title: مَرْحَبًا
cards.definition_ar: تَحِيَّةٌ عامَّةٌ تُقالُ عِندَ لِقاءِ شَخصٍ.
cards.definition_en: A general greeting used when meeting someone.

layers.concept_expansion: A common, time-neutral greeting used across Arabic-speaking contexts.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Do not restrict مرحبا to the English sense of ‘welcome’; alone it commonly means ‘hello.’
layers.connections_and_memory: Connect it with أَهْلًا and السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ as alternate greetings.
layers.transfer_prompt: Enter an evening study group and greet everyone with a time-neutral Arabic greeting.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize مَرْحَبًا in audio, give its meaning, and use it naturally without translation support.

cards.title: كَيْفَ
cards.definition_ar: اسْمُ اسْتِفْهامٍ يُسْتَعْمَلُ لِلسُّؤالِ عَنِ الحالِ أَوِ الطَّريقَةِ.
cards.definition_en: An interrogative used to ask about condition or manner: ‘how.’

layers.concept_expansion: A high-frequency question word used for manner or condition.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟ — How are you? (to a woman)
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Arabic expressions need not map word-for-word to English; كيف حالك is idiomatically ‘How are you?’
layers.connections_and_memory: كَيْفَ asks ‘how’; حال refers to state or condition.
layers.transfer_prompt: Use كَيْفَ in a greeting question, then make one other simple ‘how’ question.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize كَيْفَ in connected speech and use it productively.

cards.title: أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ
cards.definition_ar: أَنْتَ لِلْمُخاطَبِ المُفْرَدِ المُذَكَّرِ، وَأَنْتِ لِلْمُخاطَبَةِ المُفْرَدَةِ المُؤَنَّثَةِ.
cards.definition_en: أنتَ addresses one male; أنتِ addresses one female.
cards.example_en: And you? (to a man / to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: أَنْتَ = masculine singular ‘you’; أَنْتِ = feminine singular ‘you.’
layers.concept_expansion: MSA explicitly marks the gender of a singular addressee; the final vowel distinguishes these forms.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: وَأَنْتَ؟ to a man; وَأَنْتِ؟ to a woman.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Translations can hide this gender distinction, so learn the Arabic contrast directly.
layers.connections_and_memory: The same distinction appears in attached suffixes ـكَ / ـكِ.
layers.transfer_prompt: Say ‘And you?’ first to one man and then to one woman.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce and recognize both forms automatically and choose by addressee gender.

cards.title: كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟ / كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟

translations.ur: آپ کیسے ہیں؟ / آپ کیسی ہیں؟

cards.definition_ar: سُؤالٌ عَنِ الحالِ؛ ـكَ لِلْمُذَكَّرِ وَـكِ لِلْمُؤَنَّثِ.
cards.definition_en: A question about condition; use -ka for a male addressee and -ki for a female addressee.
cards.example_en: Hello, how are you? (to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: To a man: كَيْفَ حالُكَ؟ To a woman: كَيْفَ حالُكِ؟
layers.concept_expansion: حال means state/condition; the attached suffix means ‘your’: ـكَ masculine and ـكِ feminine.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: كَيْفَ حالُكَ يا مُحَمَّد؟ / كَيْفَ حالُكِ يا مَرْيَم؟
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: Without tashkeel the written forms may look identical; pronunciation still changes with the addressee.
layers.connections_and_memory: أَنْتَ/أَنْتِ and ـكَ/ـكِ encode the same gender contrast.
layers.transfer_prompt: Ask an imagined man and woman how they are, changing the suffix correctly.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce both forms correctly and explain the suffix contrast.

cards.title: بِخَيْر
cards.definition_ar: تَعْبيرٌ يَدُلُّ عَلَى أَنَّ الشَّخْصَ في حالٍ جَيِّدَةٍ.
cards.definition_en: An expression meaning that someone is doing well.

layers.concept_expansion: A concise response indicating a good state or condition.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: An explicit أنا is not required in a short answer; بِخَيْر can stand alone.
layers.connections_and_memory: The root خ-ي-ر carries the sense of goodness/well-being.
layers.transfer_prompt: Answer ‘How are you?’ naturally with a short Arabic response.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize بِخَيْر at natural speed and use it without translating first.

cards.title: الْحَمْدُ لله

translations.en: praise be to God; thank God
translations.fr: Dieu soit loué ; grâce à Dieu

cards.definition_ar: عِبارَةُ حَمْدٍ وَشُكْرٍ لله، تُسْتَعْمَلُ كَثيرًا في الحَياةِ اليَوْمِيَّةِ.
cards.definition_en: A phrase of praise and thanks to God, frequent in everyday Arabic.

layers.direct_answer: الْحَمْدُ لله = praise be to God / thank God.
layers.concept_expansion: It expresses praise and gratitude to God and occurs naturally in many everyday responses.
layers.worked_or_physical_example: بِخَيْر، الْحَمْدُ لله. — Fine, thank God.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: It is not merely a generic equivalent of ‘thanks’; the praise/thanks is directed to God.
layers.connections_and_memory: The root ح-م-د connects to حَمْد and names such as مُحَمَّد and أَحْمَد.
layers.transfer_prompt: Use الْحَمْدُ لله after stating that you are well.
layers.mastery_evidence: Understand it immediately in audio and use it appropriately in a new context.

cards.title: وَأَنْتَ؟ / وَأَنْتِ؟
cards.definition_ar: سُؤالٌ قَصيرٌ يُعيدُ السُّؤالَ إِلى المُخاطَبِ.
cards.definition_en: A short phrase that returns a question to the other person.
cards.example_en: I'm fine, and you? (to a woman)

layers.direct_answer: To a man: وَأَنْتَ؟ To a woman: وَأَنْتِ؟
layers.concept_expansion: وَ means ‘and’; the pronoun changes with the addressee’s gender.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: The two forms are not pronounced identically; the final vowel matters in MSA.
layers.connections_and_memory: This reuses the same أَنْتَ / أَنْتِ contrast found in second-person grammar.
layers.transfer_prompt: Answer ‘I’m fine, and you?’ first to a man and then to a woman.
layers.mastery_evidence: Produce both versions smoothly inside a greeting exchange.

cards.title: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ / وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام

translations.en: Peace be upon you / And upon you be peace
translations.fr: Que la paix soit sur vous / Et sur vous la paix

cards.definition_ar: تَحِيَّةٌ شائِعَةٌ، وَجَوابُها المَأْلوفُ وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام.
cards.definition_en: A common greeting meaning ‘Peace be upon you,’ with the conventional response ‘And upon you be peace.’
cards.example_en: Peace be upon you. — And upon you be peace.

layers.direct_answer: Greeting: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. Response: وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَام.
layers.concept_expansion: A highly common greeting-response pair used across formal and everyday settings.
layers.boundaries_and_misconceptions: The conventional answer begins وَعَلَيْكُمُ; do not simply echo the greeting unchanged.
layers.connections_and_memory: Root س-ل-م connects the greeting with سَلام ‘peace.’
layers.transfer_prompt: Hear the greeting unexpectedly and give its conventional response immediately.
layers.mastery_evidence: Recognize the greeting at natural speed and produce the reply automatically.
